items.text: Reverb tail no longer carries the slider morph. Changing the tail rebuilds the reverb, which waits for the slider to stop, so a swinging Tail did nothing you could hear and then rebuilt the reverb when it stopped. The other sliders keep the morph.

Tempo drift is now visible. It was working (it picks a new tempo at every pass of the lines, up to the percentage you set), but the tempo readout only ever showed the tempo you set. While the robot plays and the tempo drifts, the readout now shows the tempo that is actually playing, in the accent color. Stopped, or with drift at 0, it shows your set tempo. Note that drift only happens while the robot plays, and the tempo changes once per pass, so a slow tempo on a big grid drifts slowly.

The "clear the score" button (the slashed circle under the cube on the right rail) now shows only in edit mode, or while your finger plays the Field (where it clears field sounds). In normal play it is gone, so the "let go of all held notes" X can appear without pushing the rail down behind the tempo bar.

Always-on rows and columns now keep sounding when the robot is off. They play on their own steady pulse at the tempo (an eighth at a time), and the robot takes over when you press play. It starts once you have touched the page (the browser needs a touch before it will make sound), and it stays quiet while you are in the pencil's edit mode.
The Wander section's title is now just "Wander".

Fixed: the + on the slider handles in the Index was not showing, and the Copy and Paste icons in the morph section came out as a big dark block that clashed with the mixer. The + is back on every handle and the icons are small and sit at the end of the note line.

Slider morph, refined. The value next to a slider in the Index turns to the accent color when it is not the default. Speed now follows the tempo: Slow, Medium and Fast are 32, 8 and 2 beats a swing, so a faster tempo gives a shorter swing and a slower tempo a longer one. The slider's handle is no longer cropped at the far right edge of the Index.
Pressing any other control closes the open morph section.
Copy and Paste icons in the morph section carry one slider's motion, speed and span to another.
The slider morph is now part of the shared kit (Surface) so every tool can use it.

Morph on a slider. In the Index, the handles of the continuous sound and dice sliders (Favourite holds, Repeat the step before, Air, Space, Tail, Timbre, Grain, Morph, Tempo drifts, Holds and repeats, Pauses) now carry a +. Hold the handle and the slider stays put while a section opens below with Motion (Still, Ping-pong, Sweep, Drift), Speed (Slow, Medium, Fast) and Span (Small, Wide, Full). The + turns to a - while it is open, hold again to close. The handle's mark is grey, and turns to the accent while the slider is set to move. Two dots on the track show the reach of the swing, a faint one marks the centre. Drag the slider, or double-tap its name, and the swing re-centres there. Your settings are kept.
Structural sliders (Size, Colours, Tempo) have no morph. The heads-up display sliders do not have it yet.
